title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE RESTORATION OF HONOR OF AND COMPENSATION TO PERSONS RELATED TO THE BUSAN-MASAN DEMOCRATIC UPRISING
title_original: 부마민주항쟁 관련자의 명예회복 및 보상 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Diseases related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising) "Disease prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2(2)c of the Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means a disease newly incurred or aggravated as a direct or indirect result of injury, being wanted by investigative authorities, being taken into custody, or detention related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, which is recognized by the Deliberative Commission for Ascertaining the Truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising and Restoring the Honor of Related Persons under Article 4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission").

Article 3 (Functions of Commission) (1) When the Commission makes a determination on the restoration of honor under Article 4(2)6 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "restoration of honor") and deems it necessary, it may recommend to the President measures for the restoration of honor of a related person.
  (2) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4(2)8 of the Act means the following matters:
  1. Matters concerning support for foundations related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising under Article 16 of the Act;
  2. Matters concerning plans for utilizing donated money and goods under Article 17 of the Act;
  3. Other matters that the Commission deems necessary in relation to ascertaining the truth, restoration of honor, compensation, etc.

Article 4 (Operation of Commission) (1) The Chairperson of the Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Chairperson") shall convene meetings of the Commission and preside over them.
  (2) If the Chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to unavoidable circumstances, a member predesignated by the Chairperson shall act on behalf of the Chairperson.
  (3) When the Chairperson intends to convoke a meeting, he or she shall notify each member of the date, time, place, and agenda items of the meeting no later than 3 days before the meeting is held.
  (4) A majority of the members of the Commission shall constitute a quorum, and any decision thereof shall require the concurring vote of at least a majority of those present.

Article 5 (Disqualification, challenge, and recusal of members) (1) Where a member falls under any of the following cases, he or she shall be disqualified from participating in deliberation and resolution on the relevant agenda item:
  1. Where a member or his or her spouse or former spouse becomes a party to the relevant agenda item or is a joint right holder with a party to the agenda item;
  2. Where a member is or was a relative of a party to the relevant agenda item;
  3. Where a member is a witness or person for reference under Article 9(1) of the Act in relation to the relevant agenda item;
  4. Where a member or a corporation, organization, etc. to which the member belongs is or was the agent of a party to the relevant agenda item.
  (2) An applicant, a reporting party, or a person subject to an investigation may file a request for challenge with the Commission where there are circumstances under which it is impracticable to expect fairness in deliberation or resolution by a member, and the Commission shall make a determination thereon by resolution. In such cases, the member who is the subject of the application for challenge shall not participate in the resolution.
  (3) If a member falls under any ground for disqualification under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the member shall notify the Commission of such fact and shall recuse himself or herself from the deliberation and resolution of the relevant agenda item.

Article 6 (Standing members) The standing members under Article 5(1) of the Act shall be appointed by the President from among any of the following persons:
  1. A person who has held office as a judge, prosecutor, military judicial officer, or attorney-at-law for not less than 5 years;
  2. A person who has held office as an associate professor or higher at an accredited university for not less than 8 years;
  3. A person who holds or held office as a public official of Grade II or higher or a public official belonging to the Senior Executive Service, and has been in public service for not less than 5 years;
  4. A person who has not less than 8 years of research activities or experience related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising.

Article 7 (Administrative staff of Commission) (1) The Commission shall have 1 executive secretary and such employees as necessary to process its business affairs.
  (2) The executive secretary shall be appointed by the Chairperson from among public officials of Grade III of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety or public officials in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (3) The employees assigned to the Commission under paragraph (1) may be filled by public officials seconded from relevant central administrative agencies or local governments and by public officials in fixed-term positions; provided, if public officials in fixed-term positions are appointed, persons having extensive experience and expertise relating to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising may be given priority in employment.
  (4) The executive secretary shall process the business affairs of the Commission under the direction of the Chairperson and may attend meetings of the Commission and state opinions.

Article 8 (Establishment of working committees) (1) In order to conduct a preliminary review of agenda items to be deliberated and resolved by the Commission, and to handle matters delegated by the Commission, the following working committees (hereinafter referred to as "each working committee") shall be established under the Commission:
  1. The Working Committee on Ascertaining the Truth and Preparing Reports;
  2. The Working Committee on Examination of Status as Related Persons and Bereaved Family Members;
  3. The Working Committee on Disability Ratings.
  (2) Each working committee under paragraph (1)1 and 2 shall be comprised, with due consideration given to gender balance, of not more than 10 members appointed or commissioned by the Chairperson from among persons having extensive experience or expertise relating to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising. In such cases, 3 persons recommended by the relevant organizations referred to in Article 5(2) of the Act shall be included.
  (3) The Working Committee on Disability Ratings under paragraph (1)3 shall be comprised, with due consideration given to gender balance, of not more than 10 members appointed by the Chairperson from among persons qualified as medical specialists under Article 77 of the Medical Service Act. In such cases, 3 persons recommended by the relevant organizations referred to in Article 5(2) of the Act shall be included.
  (4) The chairperson of each working committee shall be elected by and from among its members.
  (5) The term of office of the members of each working committee shall be 2 years.
  (6) Article 4 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the operation of each working committee, and Article 5 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the disqualification, challenge, and recusal of the members of each working committee. In such cases, "Commission" shall be construed as "each working committee," and "member" as "a member of each working committee."

Article 9 (Matters necessary for operation of Commission) (1) Members attending the Commission and each working committee may be paid allowances and travel expenses within the budget; provided, this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends a meeting in direct connection with the business affairs under his or her jurisdiction.
  (2) Related persons, witnesses, or persons for reference who attend the Commission, etc. under Article 9(1) of the Act may be paid travel expenses and actual expenses within the budget.
  (3) Except as provided in this Decree, matters necessary for the operation of the Commission and each working committee shall be determined by the Chairperson through a resolution of the Commission.

Article 10 (Scope of persons eligible to report for ascertaining truth) (1) "Person in a kinship relationship" in Article 7(3) of the Act means a person included within the scope of relatives under Article 777 of the Civil Act.
  (2) "Person having knowledge of special facts" in Article 7(3) of the Act means a person who experienced or witnessed an incident related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising (hereafter in this Article referred to as an "incident"), a person who directly heard about the incident from a person who experienced or witnessed the incident, or a person who confirmed the incident through literature or records; provided, a person who directly heard about the incident from a person who experienced or witnessed the incident shall be limited to cases where the person who experienced or witnessed the incident is identifiable and alive, thereby making an investigation possible; and a person who confirmed the incident through literature or records shall be limited to cases where there exist publicly credible literature or records.

Article 11 (Issuance of certificates of related persons) The certificate of a related person under Article 12(1) of the Act shall be in Form 1.

Article 12 (Recommendation for reinstatement) (1) Where the Commission recommends an employer to reinstate a related person under Article 13 of the Act, such recommendation shall include details providing that the related person shall not suffer any disadvantage in personnel administration, such as salary class, remuneration, promotion, career, and pension, due to dismissal.
  (2) If there is no employer under Article 13 of the Act, the Commission may recommend to the President that the Government or a Government-affiliated organization employ the related person or arrange employment for the related person.

Article 13 (Examples of discriminatory treatment and disadvantageous acts) Discriminatory treatment or disadvantages under Article 15 of the Act shall include restrictions on employment, refusal to issue passports, discriminatory treatment in the execution of a sentence, and personnel disadvantages.

Article 14 (Support for foundations related to Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising) (1) The projects of a foundation for which the Government may provide necessary expenses or contribute funds under Article 16(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. Projects for commemorating related persons, including the establishment of memorial facilities for the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  2. Welfare projects for related persons and bereaved family members of the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  3. Cultural and academic projects related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  4. Other projects related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising as prescribed by the articles of incorporation of the foundation.
  (2) If a foundation intends to apply for support for project expenses, etc. under Article 16(2) of the Act, it shall submit the following documents:
  1. Articles of incorporation;
  2. Minutes of the board of directors meeting for the relevant year, including the budget and settlement of accounts;
  3. Business plans.
  (3) If any important matter determined by the Chairperson following a resolution of the Commission among the articles of incorporation or business plans is amended after a foundation has applied for support for project expenses, etc. under paragraph (2), the foundation shall submit the amended articles of incorporation or amended business plans.

Article 15 (Receipt and use of donated money and goods) (1) Where the Commission receives donated money and goods under Article 17(1) of the Act, it shall issue a receipt to the donor; provided, if a donation is made anonymously or the donor cannot be identified, a receipt may not be issued.
  (2) If a donor referred to in paragraph (1) designates the purpose for which the donated money and goods are to be used, the Commission shall use the donated money and goods solely for that purpose; provided, if there is a special reason making it impracticable to use the donation for the purpose designated by the donor, the Commission may use it for another purpose with the donor's consent.
  (3) The Commission shall keep books concerning the receipt and use of donated money and goods and shall make them available for inspection by donors.

Article 16 (Application of average wages) (1) When no evidentiary materials exist concerning average wages under Article 21(3) of the Act, the monthly wage amount or daily labor wage based on nationwide statistics by gender surveyed for each type of occupation by a wage survey institution that periodically publicizes wage statistics at least once every year shall be deemed the average wage.
  (2) In applying paragraph (1), the average wage shall first be based on the statistics in the Report on the Survey of Labor Conditions by Employment Type of the Ministry of Employment and Labor; where the Report on the Survey of Labor Conditions by Employment Type is unavailable, it shall be based on the construction wage unit price statistics of the Ministry of Data and Statistics; and where the construction wage unit price statistics are also unavailable, it shall be based on the monthly wage amount or daily labor wage of an ordinary laborer by gender surveyed through a publicly credible method; provided, the lower limit of wages shall be the average wage by gender for the year 1979 based on the statistics in the Report on the Survey of Wage Conditions by Type of Occupation. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 17 (Deduction of living expenses) "Living expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 21(4) of the Act means the amount calculated by multiplying the monthly wage amount, monthly take-home pay, or average wage by the applicable living expense ratio specified in the following subparagraphs; in such cases, whether a person has a duty of support and the scope of dependent family members shall be governed by the Civil Act:
  1. A person without dependent family members: 35 percent;
  2. A person with dependent family members: 30 percent.

Article 18 (Employable period, physical disability ratings, and rate of loss of working capacity) (1) The employable period under Article 21(5) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 1, and physical disability ratings and the rate of loss of working capacity shall be as specified in Appendix 2.
  (2) If there are 2 parts of the body affected by physical disabilities, a rating for each affected part shall first be determined in accordance with Appendix 2, and a composite evaluation rating shall then be determined in accordance with Appendix 3.
  (3) If there are 3 or more parts of the body affected by physical disabilities, a composite evaluation rating shall first be determined for the 2 most severely affected parts in accordance with Appendix 3, and the final rating shall then be determined by further evaluating such composite evaluation rating together with the highest-rated remaining affected part in accordance with Appendix 3.
  (4) Where the 3 or more most severely affected parts of the body each fall under Grade 14 of the physical disability ratings specified in Appendix 2, the disability rating shall be Grade 13 of the physical disability ratings specified in Appendix 2.
  (5) Where a person who has been notified by the Commission to undergo a medical examination at a national general hospital, a hospital affiliated with a college of medicine (excluding branch hospitals), or a hospital designated by the Commission (hereinafter referred to as "designated hospitals, etc.") for the purpose of a disability rating determination fails to undergo the examination within 1 year from the date of such notification, the Commission may determine that person's disability rating as unrated. In such cases, the Commission shall notify the person 3 months before making such determination that the disability rating may be determined as unrated and shall provide a final opportunity to undergo the examination.

Article 18-2 (Adjustment and payment of monetary compensation) (1) Monetary compensation to be adjusted and paid under Article 21-2 of the Act shall be as follows; provided, if monetary compensation has already been paid, the amount so paid shall be deducted:
  1. Where monetary compensation is adjusted and paid to the bereaved family members of a person who died or was confirmed missing in relation to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising: An amount calculated by multiplying the standard wage at the time the Commission determines to adjust and pay monetary compensation (referring to the monthly converted amount of the minimum wage publicly notified under Article 10(1) of the Minimum Wage Act; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) by the Hoffmann coefficient by age specified in Appendix 1;
  2. Where monetary compensation is adjusted and paid to a person who sustained an injury in relation to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising or to his or her bereaved family members: An amount calculated by multiplying the standard wage at the time the Commission determines to adjust and pay monetary compensation by the Hoffmann coefficient by age specified in Appendix 1 and the rate of loss of working capacity specified in Appendix 2.
  (2) In calculating monetary compensation to be adjusted and paid under paragraph (1), the statutory interest rate under Article 21(1) of the Act and the deduction of living expenses under Article 21(4) of the Act shall not apply.
  (3) Monetary compensation shall be adjusted and paid only where monetary compensation calculated under Article 21 of the Act (excluding the amount under Article 21(1)2a of the Act) is less than monetary compensation calculated under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1).
  [This Article Added on Aug. 29, 2016]

Article 19 (Livelihood support grants) (1) A livelihood support grant payable to a person falling under Article 22(1)1 of the Act or his or her bereaved family members shall be an amount obtained by multiplying the number of days of detention by the standard median income, within the limit of 50 million won. In such cases, the standard median income shall be the amount obtained by dividing by 30 days an amount equivalent to 40/100 of the standard median income (referring the standard median income for a 4-person household) under subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the National Basic Living Security Act for the year in which the payment of the livelihood support grant is determined. <Amended on Nov. 30, 2015>
  (2) A livelihood support grant payable to a person falling under Article 22(1)2 of the Act or his or her bereaved family members shall be 4.8 million won.
  (3) A livelihood support grant payable to a person falling under Article 22(1)3 of the Act or his or her bereaved family members shall be the amount payable under the standards specified in Appendix 4 for the period of removal from office recognized by the Commission; in such cases, the period of removal from office and mandatory retirement age shall be determined in accordance with the following standards:
  1. The period of removal from office shall be the period from the date on which a person was removed from office from the relevant workplace to the day preceding the mandatory retirement date, reinstatement date, or special employment date, and, for a person who has not reached the mandatory retirement age, the ending date of the period of removal from office shall be 6 months after he or she is determined to be a related person or bereaved family member; provided, a period during which the person served in the same or a similar occupation for at least 1 year may be excluded from the period of removal from office, and the specific standards for the same or a similar occupation shall be determined by the Commission;
  2. The mandatory retirement age shall be 55 years of age; provided, an exception may be made where evidentiary materials concerning the mandatory retirement age of the relevant workplace is submitted.
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (3), no livelihood support grant shall be paid in any of the following cases: <Amended on May 28, 2014; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Where a person's annual household income for the year preceding the application for a livelihood support grant exceeds the annual aggregate of the monthly average household expenditure by household size of urban worker households in the preceding year's household survey under designated statistics publicly notified by the Commissioner of the Ministry of Data and Statistics under Article 17 of the Statistics Act;
  2. Where, as of the date this Decree enters into force, a person has served for at least 1 year in any of the following positions:
  a. Public official in career service under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act who are Grade V or higher public official in general service (including public official in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service), and public official in special service receiving treatment equivalent to the appointment grades of Grade V or higher (including public official in general service belonging to the Senior Executive Service) under the career standards table by prospective grade for career-based competitive recruitment examinations, etc. under Article 27(3) of the Decree on Public Officials Appointment Examinations;
  b. Among public official in non-career service under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act, public official in political service, public official in extraordinary civil service equivalent to Grade V or higher (including those in the Senior Executive Service), general contract-based public officials with annual salary grade 5 or higher and professional contract-based public officials of Grade B or higher among contract-based public officials under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 35 of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations, and full-time local contract-based public officials with annual salary grade 4 or higher and of Grade B or higher among local contract-based public officials under Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act and Article 34 of the Local Public Officials Remuneration Regulations;
  c. Executive officers of public institutions falling under subparagraph 3c of Article 2 of the Official Information Disclosure Act and Article subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act.
  (5) Where a person falls under two or more of the subparagraphs of Article 22(1) of the Act, the amount most favorable to the recipient may be selected and paid.

Article 20 (Medical support grants) Medical support grants, including future medical expenses, nursing expenses, expenses for the purchase of assistive devices under Article 23(1) and (3) of the Act, and medical expenses already paid, shall be calculated in accordance with the following methods: <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. Future medical expenses: An amount calculated based on an estimate of medical expenses issued by a designated hospital, etc.; provided, where a designated hospital, etc. recognizes the necessity of future medical treatment but is unable to estimate future medical expenses, the amount determined by the Commission in consideration of the opinion of the Working Committee on Disability Ratings under Article 8(1)3 and future medical expenses awarded in similar cases;
  2. Nursing expenses: Where, based on a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc., a related person is recognized as having a physical disability even after recovery and therefore having difficulty engaging in activities without the assistance of another person, an amount obtained by multiplying the amount determined by the Commission, within the scope of the nursing allowance under Article 26 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, in consideration of the opinion of the Working Committee on Disability Ratings under Article 8(1)3, by the average remaining life expectancy published by the Ministry of Data and Statistics as of December 5, 2013.
  3. Expenses for the purchase of assistive devices: Where, based on a medical certificate issued by a designated hospital, etc., the use of assistive devices is recognized as necessary, an amount obtained by multiplying the market purchase price by the number of purchases recognized as necessary during the average remaining life expectancy referred to in subparagraph 2 according to the service life of the assistive device;
  4. Medical expenses already paid by the injured person himself or herself [hereinafter referred to as "previously paid medical expenses"]: An amount determined by the Commission by applying only the direct medical expenses incurred in treating the relevant injury from the date of injury to the date of application for payment of previously paid medical expenses, in consideration of the amount calculated by the Working Committee on Disability Ratings under Article 8(1)3 in accordance with the following items and previously paid medical expenses awarded in similar cases; in such cases, future medical expenses shall be calculated from the day following the date of application for payment of previously paid medical expenses; provided, for a person for whom payment of monetary compensation was determined before applying for payment of previously paid medical expenses, such amount shall be determined by applying only the direct medical expenses incurred in treating the relevant injury from the date of injury to the day preceding the date of determination of payment of monetary compensation, and future medical expenses shall be calculated from the date of determination of payment of monetary compensation:
  a. Where the applicant submits invoices and receipts related to previously paid medical expenses issued by the relevant medical care institution: An amount calculated by adding interest at the statutory interest rate from the date on which the medical expenses were incurred to the date of application for payment of previously paid medical expenses to the amount recognized after determining the relationship between the applicant's out-of-pocket expenses shown on the invoices and receipts and the injury already recognized; provided, such amount shall not exceed 90 million won, and where the amount so calculated is less than the amount calculated under item b, the amount calculated under item b shall apply;
  b. Where invoices and receipts related to previously paid medical expenses cannot be submitted: An amount calculated by applying the standards specified in Appendix 5 in consideration of the injury already recognized.

Article 21 (Applications for payment of monetary compensation) (1) A person intending to apply for the payment of monetary compensation, livelihood support grants, or medical support grants under Article 24 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "monetary compensation, etc.") shall submit to the Commission, through the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Do (hereinafter referred to as a "City/Do") having jurisdiction over the applicant's address, an application for payment of monetary compensation, etc. in Form 2 (including an application in electronic document form), along with the following documents (including electronic documents): <Amended on Jul. 30, 2024>
  1. One copy of a certificate concerning family relation records of the related person or a certified copy of archived family register (to be submitted only where the relationship between the related person and the applicant cannot be verified by a certificate concerning family relation records and the applicant is a bereaved family member);
  2. One copy of the statement of payment of previously paid medical expenses in Form 3 (to be submitted only where medical support grants are applied for, along with invoices and receipts issued by a medical care institution proving the previously paid medical expenses);
  3. One copy of the designation of a representative of bereaved family members in Form 4 (to be submitted only where a representative of bereaved family members has been designated, along with a certificate of seal impression or a certificate of personal signature verification of the principal);
  4. One copy of the power of attorney for application for monetary compensation, etc. in Form 5 (to be submitted only where an application is made through a representative due to emigration, hospitalization, or any other unavoidable reason);
  5. One copy of the certificate of occupation and monthly salary amount in Form 6 (to be submitted only by a wage earner);
  6. One copy of the certificate of occupation and monthly net income in Form 7 (to be submitted only by a business income earner);
  7. One copy of evidentiary documents verifying the related person's detention and the period of detention (to be submitted only where a livelihood support grant is applied for under Article 22(1)1 of the Act);
  8. One copy of evidentiary documents verifying the related person's dismissal, period of employment, and date (or period) of dismissal (to be submitted only where a livelihood support grant is applied for under Article 22(1)3 of the Act);
  9. One copy of evidentiary materials substantiating the grounds for the application.
  (2) Where a bereaved family member applies for payment of monetary compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) and there are 2 or more heirs of the same order of succession to the estate, a representative of bereaved family members shall be designated in accordance with the designation of a representative of bereaved family members in Form 4; provided, this shall not apply where an agreement among the heirs of the same order of succession is impossible.
  (3) Where a person intending to apply for payment of monetary compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) is unable to apply in person due to emigration, hospitalization, or any other unavoidable reason, he or she may appoint an agent under the power of attorney for application for monetary compensation, etc. in Form 5, verified by the following persons according to the relevant classification:
  1. In the case of residing abroad due to emigration, etc.: The head of the overseas diplomatic mission;
  2. In the case of hospitalization: The head of the relevant medical institution;
  3. In the case of confinement in a correctional institution, etc.: The head of the relevant institution;
  4. In any other case: The head of an Eup/Myeon/Dong.
  (4) If the Commission receives an application for payment of monetary compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) and any of the relevant documents specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) are not attached, it shall require the applicant to supplement them.
  (5) The Commission that receives an application for payment of monetary compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) shall verify the applicant's resident registration record through administrative data matching under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act; provided, if the applicant does not consent to such verification, the applicant shall be required to attach the relevant document.

Article 22 (Application for restoration of honor) (1) A person intending to apply for specific measures for the restoration of honor shall submit to the Commission, through the City/Do having jurisdiction over the applicant's address, an application for restoration of honor in Form 8 (including an application in electronic document form), along with the following documents (including electronic documents):
  1. One copy of a certificate concerning family relation records of the related person or a certified copy of archived family register (to be submitted only where the relationship between the related person and the applicant cannot be verified by a certificate concerning family relation records and the applicant is a bereaved family member);
  2. One copy of evidentiary materials substantiating the grounds for the application.
  (2) Article 21(3) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis to procedures for applying for restoration of honor under paragraph (1). In such cases, "payment of monetary compensation, etc." shall be construed as "restoration of honor."

Article 23 (Receipt of applications and preliminary fact-finding investigation) (1) Applications under Articles 21 and 22 shall be received by the City/Do having jurisdiction over the applicant's address.
  (2) In connection with applications received under paragraph (1), the Commission may request the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, the head of a Si/Gun, or the head of an autonomous Gu having jurisdiction over the applicant's address to conduct a fact-finding investigation under Article 9(1) of the Act.

Article 24 (Determinations) (1) When the Commission makes a determination on the payment of monetary compensation, etc. or the restoration of honor, it shall be based on reliable evidentiary materials.
  (2) Where the Commission makes a determination on compensation, a determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or a determination on the restoration of honor, it shall prepare a written determination on compensation, a written determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or a written determination on the restoration of honor in Form 9, and all members present at the Commission shall affix their names and seals thereto.

Article 25 (Notification) (1) When the Commission makes a determination on compensation, a determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or a determination on the restoration of honor, it shall retain the original copy of the written determination on compensation, the written determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or the written determination on the restoration of honor, and serve upon the applicant two authentic copies thereof and a notice of determination on compensation, a notice of determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or a notice of determination on the restoration of honor in Form 10. In such cases, where the applicant has an agent, such documents shall be served upon the agent, and one certified copy of the written determination on compensation, the written determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or the written determination on the restoration of honor shall be served upon the applicant.
  (2) The original copy of the written determination on compensation, the written determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant, or the written determination on the restoration of honor under the former part of paragraph (1) may be retained as an electronic document or a digitized document under Article 5 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. <Added on Nov. 12, 2024>
  (3) When the Commission determines to make a recommendation under Articles 13 and 14 of the Act, it shall notify the applicant thereof, and where the applicant has an agent, it shall notify the agent thereof. <Amended on Nov. 12, 2024>

Article 26 (Application for redeliberation) A person intending to apply for redeliberation under Article 27 of the Act shall submit to the Commission an application for redeliberation in Form 11, along with the following documents:
  1. One copy of a medical certificate of physical (mental) disability in Form 12 issued by a designated hospital, etc. (to be submitted only where there is an objection to the determination of a disability rating);
  2. One copy of documents proving the number of days of detention issued by a publicly credible institution, such as a police station, a detention house, or a correctional institution (to be submitted only where there is an objection to the calculation of the number of days of detention);
  3. One copy of documents proving the period of removal from office, such as the articles of incorporation or company regulations of the relevant workplace (to be submitted only where there is an objection to the calculation of the period of removal from office);
  4. One copy of other materials proving the grounds for redeliberation.

Article 27 (Disclosure of materials) Where an applicant or a person authorized by the applicant requests disclosure of materials related to the review, the Commission may disclose the relevant materials under the Official Information Disclosure Act and the Personal Information Protection Act.

Article 28 (Consent and claim for payment) Where an applicant who has received a notice of determination on compensation or a notice of determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant under Article 25(1) intends to receive monetary compensation, etc., he or she shall submit to the Commission a written consent and claim in Form 13, along with the following documents: <Amended on Jul. 30, 2024>
  1. One authentic copy of the written determination on compensation or the written determination on the payment of a livelihood support grant;
  2. One copy of the applicant's certificate of seal impression or certificate of personal signature verification;
  3. One copy of the passbook of a financial institution account to which monetary compensation, etc. may be paid.

Article 29 (Paying agency) Monetary compensation, etc. determined by the Commission shall be paid by the Commission; provided, the administrative handling thereof may be entrusted to the National Treasury (including national treasury agents).

Article 30 (Time of payment) Monetary compensation, etc. shall be paid within 15 days from the date on which a claim for payment under Article 28 is filed.

Article 31 (Public notice) The Chairperson of the Commission shall publicly announce the following matters concerning applications for compensation and restoration of honor in the Official Gazette, and may also publicly announce such matters in 2 or more daily newspapers, on websites, through broadcasting, or by other means: <Amended on Nov. 24, 2020>
  1. Eligible persons;
  2. Qualifications of applicants;
  3. Institutions receiving applications;
  4. Application period;
  5. Documents to be submitted;
  6. Standards for calculating payment amounts;
  7. Procedures for deliberation and determination;
  8. Other matters necessary for application and payment.

Article 32 (Criteria for imposition of administrative fines) The criteria for the imposition of administrative fines under Article 36(1) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 6.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 8, 2020]
